wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Mines struck tankers in the Strait of Hormuz as Trump signalled he would not resume the war unless provoked, and a UN official warned 45 million people could face acute hunger if fertiliser cargoes stay blocked. Days earlier Iran's Assembly of Experts urged leaving the nuclear treaty, while the IAEA demanded its inspectors return.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: Iran's navy confirmed a mine strike that set oil tankers ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz, and the Houthis now hold the Red Sea's southern chokepoint, so both sea lanes around Arabia carry risk. Brent jumped to $94.30 minutes after Trump's Iran post said there was no need for a deal, while Saudi Arabia pumped 10.56 million barrels a day in October.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: WTI trades alongside Brent, and both slid in early November on Iran diplomacy and Saudi Arabia's report of October output up 26%; the IEA says the market is returning to surplus for the first time since the Iran war began. The rebound came when Trump posted there was no need for an Iran deal, and a day later a tanker hit a mine in east Hormuz.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: An LNG carrier exploded on a mine in Hormuz, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was struck, and Pakistan rationed gas as the Iran war squeezed Gulf supply. US gas trades on its own domestic market, and none of these reports ties the Gulf disruption to its price.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: The latest wheat news postdates this monthly price: Israel's war left 24% of Lebanon's wheatland fallow, the UN urged Iran and the US to let fertilisers through Hormuz, and wheat fell on hopes that trilateral talks would free up the Black Sea. None of it explains the earlier rise.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.
rice.recent: The fortnight's rice reporting was about the next crop rather than this one: a call for Southeast Asia to breed varieties that outlast El Niño, and a UN plea to Iran and the US to let fertilisers through Hormuz. Neither accounts for the price.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Copper fell to $13,778 a tonne in London on 6 November, its lowest since July, as a backlash against AI spending and a tech rout hit the metal, and China growth woes deepened the slide. Adani agreed to finance Codelco's Kaburkaala exploration in northern Chile, and drilling in Chagai, Balochistan, found copper and gold at eight sites.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: November's climb came as the Fed turned toward tightening again. Core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October, the Fed's Logan called for two more rate hikes, possibly rapidly, and traders priced 78% odds of a December hike. The selloff reached the short end hardest, with two-year Treasury yields jumping 18 basis points in a single night.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The Democratic sweep in the midterms hit the AI trade at the index's core: Nvidia fell 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% as a backlash against data centres turned political, and the rout spread to Asia. The next day's jobs report showed 165,000 hires in October against 65,000 forecast.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The slide bottomed in the chip sell-off after the midterms, when a backlash against data centres knocked Nvidia down 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% in one session, and the AI rout spread to Asia. A week later Nvidia took a second blow: its futures fell nearly 12% on reports its board may oust Jensen Huang.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The Iran war's oil shock priced out enough demand to cut oil emissions 1.9%, and Pakistan has now made a fifth straight cut at the pump. Valero says freight to Asia costs $30-$35 a barrel, a premium that favours US Gulf Coast refiners. The US still raised its 2027 gasoline and diesel forecasts.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Gas from the Gulf has been struggling to leave through Hormuz. ADNOC Gas is studying export routes around the disruption, and Iran's navy said an LNG carrier hit a mine in the strait. Europe bids for the same cargoes as Pakistan, where gas rationing and nighttime power cuts have already set in.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: The fortnight's US news was about rates: the Fed's Waller said he would back at least a quarter-point rate hike in December, and a US inflation report followed the next day. Both came after the peak, and nothing else in the news accounts for it.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: Gulf money and the energy bill pulled against each other. UAE investors had bought $395.7 million of Pakistan's bonds since July, dollars that prop up the rupee, while diesel still cost Rs364 a litre against a pre-war Rs281, and gas rationing and nighttime power cuts showed how much imported fuel the country pays for.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight's Nigerian money stories were about who borrowed and who took, not the rate: a witness in Ikeja told Emefiele's trial that $17 million reached him through two intermediaries, and Makinde's camp demanded a probe of 11.2 trillion naira in loans backed by 340 million barrels of future crude. Neither accounts for the naira's drift.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: Egypt's dollar income picked up as shipping returned to the Red Sea: Suez Canal revenue doubled to $724 million in October, and ONE made its first transit in 3 years. A Sisi decree then set aside 112 million square metres of Red Sea coast to cut public debt, on the model of the Ras El Hekma sale to Abu Dhabi.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: The fortnight's news from Turkey was a defence pact with Qatar, a blast that killed 16 workers at a Habaş steel plant in Aliağa, and COP31 opening in Antalya. None of it accounts for the lira's price.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight carried three days of protests that disrupted garment factories in Bangladesh, and Sheikh Hasina's application from India for a Bangladeshi passport, which Dhaka rejected. None of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah slid through a political crisis in Jakarta: three top police officers were arrested for allegedly tapping the president's phone, his chief of staff was dismissed, and 20,980 troops deployed while the government could not say who was behind it. A week later Prabowo was said to accept the resignation of his vice president.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The news from Lebanon was security and war damage. The army seized a weapons depot in Beirut's southern suburbs, a raid only TASS reported, and Israel's war left 24% of Lebanon's wheatland in the Bekaa Valley fallow. Neither explains the small moves in a currency held near a fixed rate.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: Exporters in Ningbo are already absorbing a yuan that has gained 9% on the euro, and Citi sees it strengthening to 6.5 per dollar by mid-2027. Beijing is widening the currency's reach: 19 African countries can now settle in yuan without New York or London banks, and Hong Kong's exchange launched an index of 305 offshore yuan bonds.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: October's exports jumped 30% and the trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion, meaning fewer dollars leaving India. In the same release week, retail inflation hit 6.09%, a two-year high above the central bank's ceiling, which put a rate rise on the table. Both figures came out on 13 November, after the rupee had already firmed, so neither explains the move.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The real weakened after Lula's runoff win, as Bloomberg described Brazil's investor class cooling on him. Brazil's central bank then said inflation had passed the top of its target range while growth slows, and named four shocks behind it. October consumer prices rose 4.63%, below forecasts but still above the target band, with Lula's fiscal gap unresolved.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless migrant caravans were stopped. The threat followed 1,500 migrants setting out on foot north from Tapachula. Tariffs land on the exports that earn Mexico its dollars, but the threat came after the peso's weakest point, and nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for that slide.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: Washington's intervention to defend the yen was paid for in euros: it sold $500 million of them, adding supply on the day the yen breached 160. Behind that, the race to succeed Lagarde at the European Central Bank stalled, with Germany's chancellor and finance minister rejecting each other's candidates for its executive board.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying its own currency, and Washington then sold $500 million of euros for yen as the rate pressed against the 160 line, a rare US hand in Tokyo's defence. The weakness has winners at home: nearly half of Japan's manufacturers raised their profit forecasts on it.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble rests on oil export earnings, and those held up under sanctions: Russian crude sold at a record premium above Brent as China and India kept buying. Alongside it, Russia and Ukraine opened their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi, where the US pitched a new security framework covering Europe.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The rand's slide came as local election results left 110 councils projected to hang and left parties holding 20% of the vote named their conditions for backing the ANC. It followed the US suspension of South Africa's duty-free AGOA access, which carried $1.7 billion of exports in 2025.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: After the $6.3bn Binance hack, customers pulled a net $4.72 billion from the exchange, and the CLARITY Act then stalled 49 to 50 in the Senate. Spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.282 billion in a week, MSCI dropped Strategy, owner of 850,364 bitcoin, from its indexes, and money left crypto for Anthropic's IPO.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Ethereum fell with the whole crypto market after a $6.3bn hack of Binance, which North Korea denied carrying out, and users pulled over $3 bln from the exchange. Bitcoin then broke below $75,000 and later $65,000, while Binance closed EU accounts and Senator Blumenthal's letters asked crypto firms for records by 30 November.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Gold bounced after the Democratic sweep in the US midterms pulled down the dollar and Treasury yields. It slid back below $4,000 when hot US inflation and Fed remarks turned the market toward a rate hike, which raises the cost of holding a metal that pays nothing. Chinese gold ETFs drew $784 million in October, buying the dip.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi, where the US pushed a new security framework for Europe. As they ran, a Moscow car bomb injured Sergei Zavorotny, ex-adviser to Mykola Azarov, the second in two days after St Petersburg; then Zelensky said the US had raised a Donbas withdrawal in exchange for NATO.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: The US struck Iran's Qeshm Island as an Iranian commander set out five conditions for regional security. Since then the IRGC has dictated which lane ships may use: tankers and an LNG carrier that Iran says took the southern route hit mines, and a UN official puts 45 million people at risk of acute hunger as fertiliser shipments stall.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran's Revolutionary Guards now dictate which lane ships use, and those on what they call the unauthorised southern route have hit mines: two supertankers carrying over 4 million barrels, then an LNG carrier. The blockade holds back fertiliser shipments, and a UN official warns of acute hunger for 45 million people.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Yemen's Saudi-backed government pulled its forces off the positions above the strait to defend Aden, leaving the Houthis holding both shores after months of Saudi strikes on Sanaa and Houthi missiles at Riyadh. The same week a Japanese container ship transited Bab al-Mandab for the first time in three years.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Egypt's Suez Canal earned $724 million in October, its revenue doubled by returning traffic. Then Ocean Network Express sent a ship through Bab al-Mandab for the first time in three years, the weekend Saudi-backed Yemeni forces retreated from the Red Sea and left the Houthis holding both shores of the canal's southern approach.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from the other end of the oil route. Iran's navy says a liquefied natural gas carrier exploded on a mine in Hormuz, and a third US carrier strike group, reported from Singapore, closed on the Iran war. Neither accounts for the traffic through the strait.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Xi vowed in Beijing that Taiwan would be reunified and did not mention force, the strait's one political headline of the fortnight. Nothing in the reporting accounts for the one-day collapse in ship counts and the rebound that followed it.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting concerns the canal itself. The shipping news was on the other side of the world: Ocean Network Express sent a ship through Bab al-Mandab, and Egypt's Suez Canal earned $724 million in October. None of it accounts for Panama's traffic.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Black Sea shipping is moving under fire: drones reportedly hit at least 7 ships there in a single month, and Russia struck 3 cargo ships off Odesa, claiming they carried weapons to Ukraine. The EU pledged €50 million for a Black Sea security hub. Drones then hit 3 ships in Romanian waters near Sulina, the Danube's outlet.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's reporting from the region was about Spain's politics, not its shipping: a general strike in which unions say 90% of port and auto workers walked out came after the latest reading, and nothing reported explains the October trough or the recovery since.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: A Japanese container ship crossed Bab al-Mandab after three years away. That is the kind of return to the Red Sea that pulls ships off the Cape route. The same day, the Houthis said they fired missiles at Riyadh's King Khalid Airport. Both came after the latest reading, so neither explains the recent dip.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's Black Sea news was drones striking three ships near Romania's Sulina canal, the Danube's outlet, and the Abu Dhabi peace talks. None of it concerns the Kerch Strait or accounts for its traffic.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight's news from Türkiye was a defence pact with Qatar, COP31 opening in Antalya and a blast that killed 16 Habaş steel workers in Aliağa. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Two stories came out of Malaysia in the fortnight. Najib Razak left Kajang prison for house arrest after paying a $12.3M fine. Separately, the Nvidia fallout brought scrutiny to the $94.67 billion of data centre investment Malaysia's trade ministry has approved since 2021. Neither story, as reported, accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Jakarta's fortnight was dominated by a wiretapping scandal: police detained 3 generals over the alleged tapping of the president's phone, his chief of staff was dismissed, 20,980 troops deployed in the capital, and Prabowo was said to have accepted his vice president's resignation. The slide began well before any of it, and nothing here explains it.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The slide deepened as an AI rout spread to Asia and South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. Japan then spent a record ¥7.98 trillion in one day buying yen, and Washington sold $500 million of euros to join it. Both moves propped up the weak currency that had let nearly half of Japan's manufacturers raise profit forecasts.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The past fortnight brought a run of Chinese tech listings to the city, with Alibaba's T-Head chip unit and Adaspace's orbital computing business among them, and HKEX launched its first index of offshore yuan bonds. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The fortnight's mainland reporting was about the yuan, not shares. The PBOC set a weaker fixing to slow a rally that has squeezed exporters in Ningbo, producer prices hit their highest since June 2022, and Changan's nine-month profit fell 98%. None of it was reported as the cause of the index's slide.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: A sell-off in AI stocks reached Asia in early November and hit hardest here: South Korea halted trading on a Friday after the Kospi fell 8%, with SK Hynix among the chipmakers caught in the rout. The company kept building through it, pressing on with its first fab in Yongin, designed to stand 150 metres tall.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: October was strong on the real economy: exports surged and the trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion, and carmakers dispatched an estimated 525,000 cars to dealers. Against that, retail inflation hit 6.09%, a two-year high. None of these reports ties any of it to the index's climb.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's fortnight brought a national vault for 500 tonnes of foreign central-bank gold and scrutiny of Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company tied to Nvidia's Jensen Huang, but neither reaches the banks and property firms the index is built on, and nothing else in the input explains its fall.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: An AI rout spread across Asia in early November, with South Korea halting trading after the Kospi fell 8%, and it reached TSMC. A day earlier, Micron paused work on a $4.5 billion Taiwan plant after the island's first chip-industry strike. The latest drop came as Xi pledged reunification and China staged unannounced Pacific drills.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The fortnight's news touching the market was a jump of 18 basis points in two-year Treasury yields on Fed fears, and Coles disclosing a cyber attack without saying what happened. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The news out of South Africa this fortnight was about trade and politics. The US suspended the country's AGOA duty-free access, which carried $1.7 billion of exports in 2025, and local elections left 110 councils projected to hang. Woolworths Foods reported turnover growth of 1.9%. None of it is tied to the index's path.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: After Lula's runoff, economists raised Brazil's 2027 inflation forecast to 4.76% from 4.34%. The central bank then said inflation had passed the top of its target range while growth slows, which is the case for keeping borrowing costs high. October's 4.63% reading came in below forecasts.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless migrant caravans were stopped, after 1,500 migrants set out walking north from Tapachula. That is a direct threat to the US demand this market leans on. None of the other Mexico news, a cartel arrest in Zapopan among it, accounts for the rally that came before.

mkt:byma.standing: Argentina's main stock index, on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos in Buenos Aires. Priced in pesos, which have repeatedly lost most of their value, so it rises even in bad years: daily direction counts, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The fortnight's Argentine news was Pope Leo's tour, Javier Milei's refusal to recognise Lula's election win, and Iran listing Argentina's navy and air force as terrorist organisations. None of it touches the economy or the listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Enbridge's quarterly profit rose on its natural gas businesses, and Barrick Mining filed to take its North American gold assets public. Carney said Canada could work with Chinese automakers if US trade talks fail. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Two-year Treasury yields jumped 18 basis points overnight as traders priced in a half-point Fed hike. A day later Nvidia futures fell nearly 12% on reports its board might oust Jensen Huang, who then quit, leaving Colette Kress as interim CEO. Anthropic's listing, six times oversubscribed, seeks up to $90.4 billion.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Oil producers weigh heavily in the index: Brent jumped to $94.30 minutes after Trump's Iran post, and analysts expect eight oil majors to make over $350bn in operating cash from the war. The Bank of England raised rates against an inflation peak it forecasts at 4.9%, and Bailey called a second hike more likely than not if the war goes on.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The news out of Germany ran against a rise rather than behind one. Mercedes-Benz halted investment in Germany after four months of talks, and Nagel backed a third ECB rate hike this year, in December. Neither explains the index's climb, and nothing else in the input does.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The fortnight in France was political and social. Mélenchon promised nationalisations and a NATO exit at Le Bourget, unions struck for wages, and a fifth weekend of cost-of-living protests ended with 219 arrests. Prosecutors blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards for hacking 700 French supermarkets. None of it is tied to the index's move.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Dutch news through the period was about who replaces Christine Lagarde at the European Central Bank, a race down to Knot and De Cos, and about 15,498 Dutch firms queuing for grid capacity as data centres crowd out warehouses. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain staged its first general strike in 14 years over rents, with unions saying 90% of port and auto workers walked out. In Brussels, Knot and De Cos became the only two candidates to replace Lagarde at the European Central Bank. Neither event accounts for the index's path.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: Italy wants €5.9 billion from its banks next year, and Intesa has publicly attacked the levy. That is a direct charge on the lenders that weigh most in this index. But it came weeks after the autumn trough, and nothing in the record from that time accounts for the earlier fall.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The news out of Switzerland in this stretch was the franc gaining against the dollar alongside the yen after the US midterms, and Swiss inflation accelerating to its highest in almost three years. Neither explains the index's climb, since a firmer franc cuts what its big exporters earn abroad.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The slide into early November came as Trump announced an end to $4 billion a year in US aid to Israel after 2026, with the political deadlock leaving no majority to govern. Eisenkot, given 28 days to form a government, is now negotiating a unity deal with Netanyahu, who still commands the security services as caretaker.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The peak came with the midterms Republicans lost, when Vance called the Iran war 'the reason we lost' and clashed with Trump over it. Since then Netanyahu has pressed him almost daily to resume striking Iran while he holds fire at the request of Gulf neighbours, and he has said he would consider military force against Cuba.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: October brought 165,000 new jobs against 65,000 forecast and core prices rose 0.3%, and the Fed's Logan then called for two more hikes, possibly rapidly. Traders put 78% odds on a December hike, and two-year Treasury yields jumped 18 basis points overnight on fears of a 50 bps move.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The ECB has turned from cutting to hiking: eurozone inflation reached 4%, its eighth straight month over target, and Nagel backed a December increase that would be the third this year. Christine Lagarde leaves on 7 February, and Knot and De Cos are the only two candidates to succeed her.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: US employers added 165,000 jobs in October against 65,000 forecast, and that hiring pace sent Treasuries lower as traders bet the Fed would raise rates again. The Fed's Barkin said the policy direction was clear but needed a careful pace, and the BLS reported that prices rose slightly in October.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Gold slipped back to near $4,000 over the same weeks, held down by hot US inflation and Fed remarks as the market looked ahead to a Fed rate hike. Higher rates weigh on metals that pay no interest, and silver tends to fall further than gold. Nothing in the input addresses silver's own supply or demand.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: October's report showed inflation slowing less than expected, and the Fed's Goolsbee called it 'borderline disturbing'. Treasuries slid as traders cemented bets on a December rate hike, and Bitcoin dropped to almost a three-month low as the data dimmed risk appetite.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Iran is now enforcing which lane ships may use: the Revolutionary Guards say tankers on what they call the illegal southern route hit mines, among them an LNG carrier and two supertankers, and that the strait stays closed until conditions are met. With fertiliser shipments stalled, a UN official puts the people at risk of acute hunger at 45 million.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Box ships through this strait are the Suez Canal's paying traffic, and Egypt's canal doubled its revenue to $724 million in October. A Japanese container ship then made its first transit in three years, the same week Yemen's government pulled its forces back to defend Aden and left the Houthis holding both shores of the strait.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Suez Canal revenue doubled to $724 million in October as ships returned to the route. Since then Yemen's government forces have withdrawn from near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis holding the Red Sea's southern chokepoint that every southbound Suez ship must pass. The same weekend, Ocean Network Express sent a ship through it for the first time in about three years.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news for Asia came from the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Guard says mines struck tankers and an LNG carrier that used what it calls an unauthorised route, and Siam Cement kept its Vietnam plastics plant shut until mid-2027. None of it accounts for the daily count here.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: Nothing reported in the fortnight accounts for the October trough. The news was about mines striking tankers in Hormuz and the Houthis taking Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea's southern chokepoint, after Yemeni government forces withdrew. Both came after the last reading.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, where the US pressed for a new security framework covering Europe. Zelensky then said the US had raised a Donbas withdrawal in exchange for NATO. The European Commission demanded Starshield be restored after its limits cut Ukraine's drones off above 161 km/h.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Nvidia's board opened an investigation into Jensen Huang over his ties to Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whose employer reportedly bought $4.8bn of Nvidia equipment. Within days he resigned and Colette Kress, finance chief since 2013, took over as interim CEO, as House committees and a shareholder lawsuit pressed the company.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: India carried Apple to a record quarter, with iPhone revenue holding up against price pressure. But the new CEO called memory-chip prices "unprecedented" and guided gross margin to 45-46%, down from 47.9%, and about $140 billion came off the company after hours. Apple is raising prices, and in China its iPhone AI now runs on Alibaba's Qwen.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Google bought $10 billion of Anthropic as the AI lab began its IPO roadshow, agreed it can take over Anthropic's $19 billion data center lease that TeraWulf borrowed against, and shipped Gemini 4 Hydrogen. None of that news accounts for the share's slide, most of which came before it.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket failed 10 minutes after liftoff from Cape Canaveral on Sunday, ending its 100% success record and destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites. The loss came after the share's last close, so nothing on the line reflects it yet.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: An outage left Outlook and Teams disrupted for nearly a day, with Downdetector logging 130,000 reports at the peak, and the shares fell 3% amid the disruptions. Days earlier the company briefly took second place by market value when Nvidia fell 6.27% on news of Huang's exit.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: VMware released vSphere Express for virtualization on up to 128 cores, and one analysis argued that Anthropic's S-1 strengthens the case for Broadcom's AI growth. Neither accounts for the share's slide.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: The trough came as SpaceX's default risk hit a fresh peak in a tech-led selloff. Since then the company has planned $74 billion of AI computing campuses, and the European Commission has demanded it restore Starshield in Ukraine, where Zelenskyy says the service caps interceptor drones at 161 kph.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: The fortnight brought fines and retreats, not results: Italy fined Meta $880m over photo privacy, Brazil fined Facebook for missed court orders during the election, and Meta shelved terms claiming AI training rights over customers' websites while readying a bond sale for AI. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: Aramco's third-quarter profit rose 9% to $31.2 billion on oil prices lifted by the Hormuz crisis, and it began expanding the East-West pipeline, its export route around the strait. Days later an unclaimed attack set that pipeline ablaze, after Houthis claimed strikes in the kingdom and missile debris blew out windows across Aramco Tower in Riyadh.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla said it would end the Cybertruck, which sold 11,586 in nine months on Cox Automotive's estimate, and turn its focus to robotics and AI; the shares jumped 4% that morning. Days later it claimed the steering-wheel-free Cybercab meets federal safety standards, without explaining how.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: The period carried Samsung's buyout talks with Modine, which sent Modine's own shares up, and its opposition, alongside Tesla, to new US tariffs on Vietnam. Neither accounts for the fall in Samsung's share.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: The trough came on the day about 12 workers in Taoyuan staged Taiwan's first chip-industry strike against Micron, and the company paused work on a $4.5 Billion Taiwan plant over the labor spat. Chip makers fell together that session after the midterms, Micron by 11%.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: AMD reported a record quarter in which data-center revenue jumped 97% to $8.55 billion while its gaming business cratered, and its sales forecast topped estimates on AI chip demand. Two days later chip stocks sold off together after the midterms, AMD by 12% alongside Nvidia and Micron.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: SK Hynix is building around the clock at Yongin, where its first fab will stand 150 metres tall, and Reuters and Bloomberg report a $1 billion five-year fund and a testing hub for smaller Korean chip suppliers. None of that accounts for the share's slide across the window.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.
us-mortgage.recent: The one related report in the fortnight was that US home sales had fallen to their lowest level since 2016, which is a result of borrowing costs, not a cause of them. Nothing in it explains why the rate moved.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.
ez-cpi.recent: October's figure came in at 4%, extending a run of eight straight months above 2%, a month beyond what the chart shows. The reporting carried the readings themselves but nothing on which prices drove them.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The slide ran alongside Bitcoin, which fell below $65,000 for the first time since August and took the wider crypto market down with it. It came despite Schroders, a $1.1 trillion manager, bringing an emerging-market bond fund onto Solana as tokenized shares earlier in the month.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: XRP fell with the rest of crypto: a Nvidia-led tech selloff, then mounting Bitcoin ETF outflows and a US inflation reading that dimmed risk appetite, left it at its lowest since November 2024. The XRP Ledger's own news was technical: a fix for a flaw that could let stablecoin partners print tokens, and a quantum plan.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: Traders on the exchange bet on stocks as well as crypto. When reports said Nvidia's board might oust Jensen Huang, Nvidia perps on Hyperliquid fell 7% while Bitcoin sat listless. Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the token's own slide.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Zcash jumped 12% in a post-election crypto rebound that kept Bitcoin above $80,000. Nothing in the input explains the slide that followed.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: The Bank of England raised rates unanimously on Nov 5, its first hike since 2023, after forecasting that Britain's inflation will peak at 4.9%. Bailey said a second hike was more likely than not if the war goes on, and on Nov 14 the Bank's chief economist said further rises were needed.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: The fortnight's stories sit around the rate rather than explaining its last step: the yen slid toward 160 per dollar and Japan spent a record ¥7.98 trillion buying it in one day, while wholesale inflation accelerated and Ueda saw 'some upside risks' to inflation, which keeps a further BOJ rate hike in view.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.
tcmb-rate.recent: The one relevant item from the fortnight is the central bank raising its end-2027 inflation forecast to 21%, published after the latest reading. A higher inflation path argues for a slower pace of cuts, but nothing in the input explains the cut itself.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The People's Bank of China's moves this fortnight were about the currency, not the cost of credit. It set a weaker yuan fixing and raised the forex deposit reserve requirement to slow a yuan rally fed by a record trade surplus, and none of that touched its lending rate.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.
bcb-rate.recent: Brazil's central bank is caught between two pressures: inflation has passed the top of its target range while growth slows. The bank names four separate shocks behind the overshoot, so it cannot ease to support a cooling economy without letting prices run further.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia raised the path it expects its key rate to follow after putting fourth-quarter inflation at 7.1-7.6%. Its case is that a higher key rate trajectory is what brings inflation to 4% in 2027, so borrowing in Russia stays dearer for longer than the bank had signalled.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index bottomed the same day Thai inflation was reported at 3.9%, above the central bank's ceiling. Days later Siam Cement, one of the exchange's heavyweights, said its core Vietnam plastics plant, shut by the Hormuz disruption, will stay closed until mid-2027. That is the regional energy shock showing up in a Thai company's operations.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi missiles have kept landing on the kingdom: a strike on Riyadh's airport killed at least 13 on 10 October, debris blew out windows across Aramco Tower, and an attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze. Aramco's third-quarter profit rose 9% to $31.2 billion on the Hormuz crisis, and the Qatar PM called U.S. talks on Iran positive.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The climb came as the US stepped back from striking Iran: Trump signalled new strikes were unnecessary after a meeting in Qatar, whose prime minister called the US talks on Iran positive. The Strait of Hormuz, the Gulf's trade artery, still let through no unauthorised vessels.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The economy weakened under it: Philippine GDP growth slowed to 2.1% in Q3, dragged by inflation, which squeezes the household spending this market leans on. The ASEAN summit in Manila then opened with the trade war in focus ahead of Trump's arrival, as visiting leaders sought trade to offset US risks.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: While the share fell, Meta was preparing a cross-border investment-grade bond sale to pay for its AI build-out. It also shelved terms that claimed training rights over its customers' websites after a backlash, and Brazil fined Facebook for missing court orders during the election. None of this accounts for a fall of this size.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent said it had expanded inference capacity for its Hy4 model tenfold as demand for its WorkBuddy agent strained the system, and on 11 Nov launched an AI search engine that indexes WeChat accounts. Neither announcement is tied in the reporting to the share's swings.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: A US probe of Alice Huang, whose employer Megaspeed reportedly bought $4.8bn of Nvidia equipment, turned into a spy scandal at the top: Jensen Huang resigned and Colette Kress, finance chief since 2013, took over. Shareholders sued, alleging investors were misled, and lawmakers pushed tougher export controls.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Google bought $10 billion of Anthropic alongside Nvidia ahead of the lab's listing, and agreed it can take over Anthropic's $19 billion data center lease with TeraWulf. It shipped Gemini 4 Hydrogen and was sued with OpenAI and Meta to freeze AI training. None of this explains the fall, most of which came earlier.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: Both sides escalated. Saudi strikes on Sanaa killed or wounded 1,039 people since 13 July, Iranian state agency Mehr reported. Houthi missiles were met with debris that blew out Aramco Tower's windows, and the Houthis claimed a strike on King Khalid Airport. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces then pulled back from the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to defend Aden.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news moved a handover closer. Trump posted that there was no need for an Iran deal, Iran's Assembly of Experts urged leaving the nuclear treaty, and UN nuclear inspectors said they do not know where Iran's Isfahan plant is, the site any handover would have to account for.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.
poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.recent: The one Nigerian campaign story of the fortnight was the attack in Gombe, where armed men blocked Isa Pantami's convoy with burning tyres. It does not concern Obi, and nothing else in the reporting accounts for the swings in what traders will pay on him.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Trump hosted Putin envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House and promised a 'big, beautiful agreement', then Russia and Ukraine opened their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi. A day later TASS carried word that Putin is not ready to make peace there, and Zelensky said the US had raised a Donbas withdrawal in exchange for NATO.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Every channel to talks narrowed at once. Trump posted that there was no need for an Iran deal, Iran's Assembly of Experts urged leaving the nuclear treaty, and UN nuclear inspectors said they do not know where the Isfahan plant is. Then Iran's Guard said 2 tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz.

poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reaches a valuation of at least $1 trillion in 2026. OpenAI is privately held, so this is a rare public wager on what the AI boom's best-known lab is worth.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gyanesh Kumar leaves office as India's Chief Election Commissioner by the deadline. The post runs national and state votes, and removal requires the same process as for a Supreme Court judge.

poly-will-helen-zille-be-the-next-mayor-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Helen Zille, the former Cape Town mayor and Western Cape premier, becomes Johannesburg's next mayor. The city council elects the mayor, so coalition deals can matter as much as the vote.

poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.standing: A Polymarket contract on Iran formally quitting the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty by 2027. The treaty lets a member leave on three months' notice, and leaving would end the legal basis for inspections of Iran's sites.
poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.recent: Iran's Assembly of Experts urged leaving the treaty, Mehr reported, and a day later UN nuclear inspectors said they do not know where Iran's Isfahan plant is. Weighing the other way, Trump has told advisers he will not resume the war on Iran unless provoked, even as mines struck tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. It asks about an invasion, a far higher bar than an air or missile strike.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Vance blamed the Iran war for the midterms, and Trump has since told advisers he will not resume the war unless provoked, after Mohammed bin Salman and Erdogan pressed him for restraint. Mines striking ships in the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's claimed downing of an Orbiter 4 drone have not changed that line.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by the close of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which is tied to whether Gulf oil reaches its importers.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Trump posted that the US had no need of an Iran deal, Iran's Assembly of Experts urged leaving the nuclear treaty, and Iran's Guards claimed a US radar in Bahrain. Then mines hit tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, and Trump signalled he would hold fire unless provoked, but neither side moved to lift the blockade.

poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Hamas ceasefire is cancelled by Dec 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reacts to fighting in Gaza and to the politics of the governments behind the truce.
poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.recent: An Israeli airstrike killed 6 people inside Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis without either side declaring the truce over. In Israel, Likud opened coalition talks with Eisenkot, whose demands include ending the war on Iran. None of the fortnight's reporting accounts for the swing in the betting.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by December 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on a waterway that Gulf energy exporters and importers depend on.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.recent: Trump posted that there was no need for an Iran deal, and Brent jumped within minutes. Meanwhile the IRGC was deciding which lanes ships may use through Hormuz. A liquefied natural gas carrier exploded on a mine there, and then two tankers hit mines on what Iran calls the illegal southern route.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its December meeting. That rate anchors short-term dollar borrowing, so bonds, mortgages and currencies worldwide reprice around it.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: October's core consumer prices rose 0.3%, and the Fed's Logan called for two more hikes, possibly rapidly. Two-year Treasury yields jumped 18 basis points overnight as hot inflation fed jumbo-hike fears, and Williams then called inflation "far too high" while Collins backed "steady, gradual" hikes.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Washington and Tehran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on the waterway that carries Gulf oil and gas to the world.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.recent: Trump posted that there was no need for an Iran deal, and Brent jumped to $94.30 within minutes. Since then mines have hit an LNG carrier and, by the IRGC's account, two tankers on what it calls the 'illegal southern route' through the Strait of Hormuz: Iran is enforcing which lane ships may use, not negotiating it.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by December 31. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes the strait, so the price is a bet on Gulf supply reopening.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Iran is enforcing which lane ships may use: tankers taking what its Revolutionary Guards call an unauthorised southern route through Hormuz have hit mines almost daily, two supertankers carrying over 4 million barrels among them, and the Guards say the strait stays shut until their conditions are met. A claimed lane deal with Oman has not reopened it.

poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Ukraine signs its EU accession treaty by 2027. Signing comes only after every negotiating chapter closes and all 27 member states agree, so the price is a bet on the pace of talks in Brussels.
poly-will-ukraine-sign-an-eu-accession-t.recent: The fortnight's Ukraine news was about ending the war, not joining the EU: Russia and Ukraine held their first peace talks in 9 months in Abu Dhabi, and Zelensky said the US raised a Donbas withdrawal in exchange for NATO entry. None of it bears directly on an accession treaty.

poly-pete-hegseth-out-as-secretary-of-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Hegseth stops being the US Secretary of Defense before the end of the year. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on reports about his standing at the Pentagon.
poly-pete-hegseth-out-as-secretary-of-de.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Polymarket was about the platform itself, chiefly Trump Jr.'s firm putting $300 million into it while he advised its rival Kalshi. None of it concerned Hegseth or the Pentagon, so nothing here accounts for the swing in this contract.

wiki-inflation.standing: The general rise in prices across an economy, usually measured by a consumer price index. Central banks set interest rates to keep it near a target, so its pace decides what borrowers and savers pay.
wiki-inflation.recent: The Bank of England hiked unanimously and forecast Britain's inflation to peak at 4.9%, with Bailey calling a second hike more likely than not if the war goes on. Then US core consumer prices rose 0.3% in October, the Fed's Logan called for two more rate hikes, and India's retail inflation hit 6.09%, a two-year high.

wiki-china.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on China each day: a rough gauge of how often the world's second-largest economy and most populous one-party state pulls general readers toward the basics.
wiki-china.recent: The fortnight's news from China centred on Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia. Chinese buyers are stockpiling its chips before an expected US crackdown, and Trump signalled he won't raise the spy scandal with Xi, who separately vowed Taiwan's reunification without mentioning force. None of it accounts for the earlier peak.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Houthis and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders will pay on the war between Yemen's Houthi movement and the kingdom ending, and so on Red Sea and Gulf oil risk.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: Both sides escalated: debris from intercepted missiles blew out Aramco Tower's windows in Riyadh, an unclaimed attack set the East-West pipeline ablaze, and the Houthis claimed a strike on King Khalid Airport, while Saudi strikes on Sanaa killed dozens. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces then quit the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Houthis on both shores.

wiki-islamic-revolutionary-guard-corps.standing: The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is Iran's parallel military, founded after the 1979 revolution and answerable to the Supreme Leader. It runs the missile force, a navy in the Gulf and a large business empire.
wiki-islamic-revolutionary-guard-corps.recent: French prosecutors said the Guards hacked freezers in 700 French supermarkets. Within days Iran named Argentina's navy and air force terrorist organisations, and US prosecutors charged three alleged Iran-backed operatives over Fairford. In Hormuz, the Guards kept reporting tankers set ablaze by mines on routes they call unauthorised.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily reads of English Wikipedia's article on the United States, one of its most-visited country pages. It rises when American power or politics becomes the world's story, not only America's.
wiki-united-states.recent: November opened with midterm losses that Vance blamed on the Iran war.
